repo_notes.content: This repository provides a lightweight, dual-implementation decoder for the Sandborg-Petersen morphological tagging schema used with Koine Greek (especially New Testament texts such as Nestle 1904 and Tischendorf 8th edition). It consists of three complementary deliverables: (1) a production-ready Python package published on PyPI, (2) a pure client-side JavaScript/HTML decoder, and (3) a live online tool hosted on GitHub Pages. The two code implementations are functionally equivalent and share the same mapping tables and decoding logic. Emphasize the distinction between the products while highlighting their parity and the easy integration paths between them.

pages.title: Overview
pages.purpose: High-level introduction to the Sandborg-Petersen Morphology Decoder. Explain what the tool does (converts compact SP tags such as N-NSF or V-PAI-3S into human-readable grammatical descriptions), why it exists, the three main ways to use it (online tool, Python package, standalone JavaScript), and the academic context. Provide clear entry points for different user types (biblical scholars, digital humanists, developers).

page_notes.content: Lead with the online tool URL (https://tonyjurg.github.io/Sandborg-Petersen-decoder/) and the ability to deep-link with ?tag=. Clearly state that Python and JavaScript implementations are distinct but equivalent. Mention PyPI package name (sandborg-petersen-decoder) and import name (sp_morph_decoder). Link to child pages for Getting Started, Architecture, and Licensing.

pages.title: Project Background, Schema & Licensing
pages.purpose: Document the academic origin of the Sandborg-Petersen schema (adapted from Ulrik Sandborg-Petersen’s descriptions for Tischendorf 8th / Nestle 1904), the relationship to Robinson-like tags, citation requirements (CITATION.cff + Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.14551056), and the dual-license situation (MIT for the software; CC BY 4.0 for MACULA-derived validation data).

page_notes.content: Include the exact citation metadata, required attribution links, and a note about the NOTICE.md file. Point to the original parsing.txt document on biblicalhumanities/Nestle1904. Clarify that the decoder itself is MIT-licensed while validation datasets carry CC BY 4.0 obligations.

page_notes.content: Structure as three clear subsections. For the online tool show the ?tag= deep-link pattern. For Python show pip install + the decode_tag() one-liner and the CLI. For JavaScript point to both the published GitHub Pages version and the local javascript/SP-Morph-decode.html file.

page_notes.content: Make the dual-implementation nature prominent. Note that mapping tables and parsing order are intentionally duplicated so each implementation can stand alone.

page_notes.content: Document the “first match” strategy for POS prefixes (e.g. N-PRI before N-). Describe the different structural patterns for nouns, verbs, pronouns, and special forms (infinitives, participles, indeclinables). Provide representative examples for each major category.
